text:
Omar (ACME): Hey team — after we moved our service endpoints behind a VPCE (interface endpoint) to talk to Redwood's hosted API we see intermittent TLS failures and 502s from our app. Happens ~1-2x/min.
Sara - Support: sorry you're hitting that. Can you share curl + dig results from a host in the affected subnet?
Omar (ACME): digging in. quick outputs: 
```
$ dig api.redwood.com +short
10.0.5.12
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake error: tls: handshake failure

curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.0.5.12:443 
```
Sara - Support: thanks. Do you have VPC endpoint policy or a proxy / firewall in the egress path?
Omar (ACME): We have a security appliance (managed proxy) in the same AZ that inspects egress via TLS INSPECT. SGs are open for 443 to the endpoint. Endpoint type is interface (ENIs in the subnet). No NAT involved.
Marcus - Support Eng: curious if this is SNI/certname mismatch from split-horizon DNS. Can you `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com` and paste the cert CN/SANs?
Omar (ACME): ran that, interesting output: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = vpce-1234-abcdef.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
subject=/CN=vpce-1234-abcdef.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
issuer=/C=US/O=Amazon/OU=Amazon TLS CA 1
---
No peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 305 bytes
---
```
Ling Chen: that looks like the endpoint is terminating TLS with a cert for the AWS vpce host, not for api.redwood.com. If your proxy validates SNI vs cert name it will drop the connection.
Raj Patel: confirm: with AWS PrivateLink the NLB/fronting service can either do TLS passthrough or TLS termination. For hosted Redwood we terminate TLS at our edge and expect SNI==api.redwood.com. If the VPCE is doing TLS termination or the proxy re-terminates you can see CN=vpce-*.
Omar (ACME): so why are we seeing intermittent failures though? sometimes it works.
Marcus - Support Eng: likely two code paths: some requests take a path that preserves SNI (pass-through) and others are intercepted by the proxy doing TLS inspect and re-signing with vpce CN. Or DNS split-horizon might resolve to different endpoint IPs across subnets/AZs — some ENIs are TLS-pass and some go through the appliance.
Sara - Support: can you show `traceroute` and `tcpdump` for a failure window? Also `dig +trace` from host to confirm consistent answer.
Omar (ACME): traceroute shows traffic going to 10.0.5.12 for some requests and 10.0.5.13 for others (both ENIs). tcpdump during a failure:
```
11:22:33.123456 IP 10.0.2.45.52344 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
11:22:33.223456 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.0.2.45.52344: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
11:22:33.223900 IP 10.0.2.45.52344 > 10.0.5.12.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0
```
Raj Patel: RST after SYN-ACK — that is characteristic of an inline appliance intercepting the session post-handshake decision. If the proxy can't validate cert name it might reset or drop.
Ling Chen: as a quick repro, try forcing host header + SNI using curl `--resolve` so the client connects to the ENI IP but sends SNI/api host. Example:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.com/health
```
Omar (ACME): tried `--resolve` to 10.0.5.12, still handshake fails. But `--resolve` to 10.0.5.13 works consistently. So ENI .12 is the one returning vpce cert.
Marcus - Support Eng: that pins the problem to that endpoint ENI/.12. Two hypotheses: (1) Endpoint's NLB target/passthrough config differs in AZ, or (2) there's a regional split where some VPCE ENIs are fronted by a proxy that terminates TLS (maybe our side did a migration). We'll check our side for any canary config.
infra-bot: deploy 2026-02-18T14:03:11Z: rolling tls-edge-config update to canary pool a2 in us-east-1
Marcus - Support Eng: infra-bot shows a canary rollout earlier — @Raj can you confirm if canary changed the certificate behaviour?
Raj Patel: I see the canary: we temporarily enabled NLB TLS offload in canary pool a2 which will present the NLB cert (vpce CN) for internal-facing endpoints until the rest roll. That was a mistake — should've been passthrough. Rolling back now.
Omar (ACME): awesome — any workaround before rollback completes? We need stable API for customers.
Ling Chen: workaround options: (1) allowlist the Redwood cert issuer at your proxy so TLS inspect doesn't re-terminate / allow passthrough for api.redwood.com; (2) route all egress for api.redwood.com to the ENI IP that already works (10.0.5.13) via static route/policy; (3) temporarily disable TLS inspection for that FQDN.
Sara - Support: Omar, can you open a support ticket with your proxy vendor and ask for a bypass for `api.redwood.com` while we finish rollback? We'll notify you when rollback completes.
Omar (ACME): opening ticket now. One more question — do we need to change our VPC endpoint policy or SGs after rollback?
Marcus - Support Eng: no VPC policy/SG changes needed. This was all on our side due to the canary NLB config. We'll update here when rollback finishes.
infra-bot: deploy 2026-02-18T14:10:02Z: rollback tls-edge-config canary a2 -> stable
Raj Patel: rollback finished. Marcus: can you verify that ENI .12 now presents the api.redwood.com cert?
Marcus - Support Eng: verified from us-east egress: `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.com` now shows CN=api.redwood.com and full chain.
Omar (ACME): after rollback our app errors dropped to zero. Thank you all.
Sara - Support: glad it's resolved. We'll follow up with a postmortem of the canary gap and recommend a safer rollback plan. :thumbsup:
Omar (ACME): appreciated. tagging the proxy ticket number for records: PROXY-4521
Ling Chen: we'll add a note to docs about how TLS termination + VPCE can interact with inline TLS inspection and suggested diagnostics (`openssl s_client -servername`, `--resolve`, tcpdump)
Marcus - Support Eng: adding runbook item: check infra-bot canary flag before enabling NLB offload for VPCE-backed services.
Sara - Support: closing thread, reopen if anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:
